items.X_desc: high when the headline juxtaposes roles, expectations, or facts that seem incompatible; low when elements reinforce one another. Does not apply without a readable contrast
items.Y_desc: high when roles, places, or actions explain named references within the headline; low when bare names, acronyms, or allusions require prior knowledge. Does not apply when no potentially unfamiliar reference appears

items.X_desc: Headlines containing visceral emotional adjectives (e.g., 'worst', 'unbearable', 'anger') score 1; purely factual headlines score 0. Does not apply to neutral headlines.
items.Y_desc: Scores high if the text uses vivid adjectives indicating extreme emotion or shock. Scores low for neutral, procedural language regarding legal or political events.

items.X_desc: Scores high when the headline explains enough background to understand why the event matters, and low when it depends on missing context; does not apply when context is unnecessary.
items.Y_desc: Scores high if the headline mentions local places, UK figures, or highly domestic issues. Scores low for distant foreign events lacking a UK hook.

items.X_desc: Headlines featuring explicit currency symbols or large numbers (e.g., '€200m') score 1; headlines without specific financial figures score 0.
items.Y_desc: Headline contains at least one hard numeric figure, number of casualties, monetary sum, or explicitly quantifies an outcome; low if no numbers are present.

items.X_desc: Scores high when the headline explicitly addresses readers or their choices, and low when it speaks only about others; does not apply without second-person or collective-reader language.
items.Y_desc: Headlines using "I", "Me", or "My" score high. Third-person institutional reports score low.

items.X_desc: high when readers can map the story to ordinary routines, safety, money, family, or identity; low when it is remote or specialized. Does not apply when the headline offers no basis for judging relevance
items.Y_desc: high when the headline supplies bounded details such as a number, location, object, or clear causal relation; low when claims are vague or generalized. Does not apply without a factual proposition

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing signature block
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with a personal sign-off: a name, initials, a handle, or a closing salutation. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Author sign-off at the end of the text
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer closes by naming or initialling themselves. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much displayed mathematics the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of set-off equation blocks. Count only; do not judge whether the mathematics is correct.
anchors.Y_name: How much the text hedges its own claims
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the frequency of 'I think', 'perhaps', 'it seems' and similar. Count only; do not judge whether the hedging is warranted.
